subject: Can recombinant genotypes be identified using poppr.msn function??

messages.author: d89993b905b0ab8c
messages.subject: Can recombinant genotypes be identified using poppr.msn function??
parts:
Hi there, 

I am using DArT data (dominant markers) to identify migrant, clonal and recombinant isolates within the same pathogen (very low genetic differences) collected from a field in three different years. I was able to identify clonal population using mlg.filter as well as a phylogenetic tree. How can I characterise between the migrant and recombinant isolates within that field? I know there are recombinants in the samples as ascospores collected from the field are also included. I am thinking that the minimum spanning network would help me identify recombinants but l am not able to analyse the plot. I have uploaded the msn plot (Provesti’s distance used) 

Any suggestions or interpretation of the plot will be highly appreciated. 


Many Thanks, 
Barsha

messages.author: d192ec4b1d416345
messages.subject: Re: [poppr] Can recombinant genotypes be identified using poppr.msn function??
parts:
Hi Barsha,

The nodes of the MSN represent genotypes and the lines connecting them represent genetic distance between these genotypes. This is constructed to represent the minimum spanning tree that connects these nodes. In your graph, you can see that a few of the nodes are overlapping other nodes. These nodes are connected, but the nature of the plotting makes it difficult to know how. It should be noted that in the current version of poppr, the size of these nodes are skewed as they are scaled by radius (as opposed to area), so larger nodes will be artificially inflated. The next version of poppr will scale these nodes by area instead (you can install the development version from github to try it out https://github.com/grunwaldlab/poppr).
